about: Proven mechanics to reuse instead of rewriting. A part lists where it lives TODAY (phase A: files stay where they are; phase B moves them here), when to use it, which test or gate proves it, and which films used it. The library holds mechanics, never looks: every film still gets its own flavour (AGENTS.md). Read this file and docs/DEFECTS.json before writing scene code, then import the part; do not copy-edit it.
howToAdd: At the end of a film (retro): a part is proven when a unit test or a gate that failed before now passes with it, and a second film could use it unchanged. Add it here with tags, useWhen, files, tests, usedIn. studio2/tests/library-index.test.mjs checks that every path exists.

parts.name: sign-text-fit
parts.useWhen: Any in-world sign or banner. kit.sign()/signTexture() already shrink or wrap text to fit; call signDistance(width, vfov) to place the camera so the whole sign fits the narrow 9:16 frame (horizontal fov is only about 36 degrees at vfov 60).

parts.name: dissolve-between-beats
parts.useWhen: Changing section (day to night, night to morning). A beat declares {dissolve: seconds}; main.update returns dissolveK and answers update(t,{outgoing:true}) with the previous beat; bootstrap blends both frames and collision-checks both. A dissolve counts from its first frame (dissolving(k) is true at k=0).

parts.name: camera-inside-solid-gate
parts.useWhen: Always on: collide.mjs fails a shot whose camera sits inside a solid prop, a decor volume (hill slab) or an actor body. Sky domes (back-face) and blocks 60 m or larger are exempt.

parts.name: night-exposure-option
parts.useWhen: Reference-style day, night, day light script. Pass camera.exposure (about 0.6 at night) so mean luminance swings by 0.2 or more between 5-second windows (reference 0.28).
parts.provenBy: luminance swing 0.27 measured on square-wheel with studio2/.tmp/lumcheck.py method (see HANDOFF)

parts.name: square-wheel-geometry
parts.useWhen: Anything rolling a polygon wheel over a matching road, or a round wheel over humps: exact poses for flat ground and hump roads (axle height constant to 1e-9).

parts.name: dig-strip
parts.useWhen: A ground strip whose heights come from a function of x and a dig progress per position, with a glowing ribbon over the changing part (the reference's golden glow along the rail). buildDigStrip(ctx,{heightFn,maxHeight,length}); setDig(progressFn,key), setGlow(xa,xb,progressFn). The film wraps it (road.mjs) with its own height function.

parts.name: cart-and-egg-rig
parts.useWhen: A cart whose pose is a function of one track coordinate u (flat before 0, hump road after), with cargo that dances, flies in ballistic arcs, lands as splats or sticks to a face. Egg flights must call poseAt(t0) with their own launch time.
parts.provenBy: collide gate pass over 1782 frames and review sheets

parts.name: villager-crowd-poses
parts.useWhen: Background people: crowdSpec(i,{palette}) (VILLAGE palette is an example, pass your film's own), crowdPose(p,t,mode,i,target) with modes idle cheer laugh clap gasp point wave, and spacedLine({n,x0,x1,z,minSpacing:.7}) which guarantees neighbours never overlap (hats overlap below 0.7 m). Keep 0.5 m clear of fixed props.

parts.name: story-clarity-audit
parts.useWhen: Before any paid voice or scene work: STORY.json needs thesis, at most 2 facts, a carrier object in 40% of beats, a plant before the reveal and the reveal at 40-80% of the film.

parts.name: studio-sound-baseline
parts.useWhen: Every film: 21 baseline sounds already stored in assets/sfx (whooshes, impacts, wood, metal, glass, cartoon pop and boing, splat, chimes, sad brass, crowd laugh/cheer/gasp, footsteps, day and night ambience beds). Use them from cues.mjs with B('id'); add only film-specific sounds in episodes/<id>/audio/effects.json. Never regenerate; requests are cached by hash. Needs the user's explicit OK to spend.

parts.name: film-retro
parts.useWhen: End of every film: node studio2/retro.mjs --episode episodes/<id> writes RETRO.md from the film's own files: gate runs and runs to the first pass (collide.mjs and render.mjs now log out/gate-history.jsonl and renders/render-history.jsonl), what failed most, the result numbers and which scene files are not in this index yet. Then log defects and promote parts.

parts.name: captions-auto
parts.useWhen: Captions of one or two words as fits the phrase (the reference shows 1-2 words per pop). Set film.json captionWords to "auto" (or 1, 2, 3 for a fixed maximum; default 3 keeps older films unchanged). Articles go with their noun, linking words stand apart, long or slow words stand alone, breaks follow punctuation and pauses.

parts.name: preflight-and-framecheck
parts.useWhen: Before every full render run node studio2/preflight.mjs --episode episodes/<id>: unit tests, story audit, collision gate, a one-frame-per-second sample render, flat or black frames, shots that are mostly sky, one-frame flashes, day-night brightness swing and parity with the reference, in one command. After assembling run node studio2/framecheck.mjs on out/final.mp4.

parts.name: cover-depth-of-field
parts.useWhen: Cover frame staged from the film's hook moment: coverDof(cameraPosition, facePosition) returns the engine's focus, aperture and maxblur so the far background blurs for real while the face and key prop stay sharp. Put the result into the camera options.

parts.name: finish-chain
parts.useWhen: End of every film, after the full render: node studio2/finish.mjs --episode episodes/<id> runs unit tests, collision gate, assemble, frame check and retro in the right order, stops at the first failure and prints package notes (file too big for a phone, missing cover files).

parts.name: camera-whip-pan-check
parts.useWhen: Automatic: the collision gate records the camera path (out/collide.json cameras) and preflight.mjs fails a run of fast frames that turns the view 45 degrees or more. A single-frame jump is a cut and a quick small move is allowed.

parts.name: render-smart
parts.useWhen: After the first full render, whenever code, camera, light or captions change: node studio2/render-smart.mjs --episode episodes/<id> renders a 2 fps sample, compares with renders/full and re-renders only the stretches that differ (proved: 75 deleted frames restored in 0.6 min instead of 9, identical to the original). --against DIR --dry shows what a change touches. Audio-only changes need only assemble.mjs.

parts.name: asset-catalogue
parts.useWhen: Before generating a sound or music or writing a prop: node studio2/catalog-assets.mjs --find "egg splat" [--kind sfx|music|prop] searches every film's sounds, scores and prop builders (assets/CATALOG.json, rebuilt with the same command after a film). The props picture is studio2/library/catalog/props-square-wheel.jpg, made with studio2/library/props-sheet.mjs.

parts.name: cheap-looking
parts.useWhen: Look at one preflight sheet (out/preflight-sheet.jpg, the whole film) or studio2/sheet.py output instead of frames one by one; shrink a single frame with studio2/shrink.py before looking.

parts.name: channel-registry
parts.useWhen: Several YouTube channels, one toolchain: channels/<id>/channel.json (validated) holds story profile, footer, hashtags, disclosure, voice, flavour; film.json names its channel; new-episode.mjs requires --channel; the briefing lists films per channel and flags unassigned or unknown ones.

parts.name: survival-story-profile
parts.useWhen: Film of the channel post-time-survival: story-audit.mjs applies auditSurvival (protagonist, threat, stakes, rule, ending; danger 1-5 on every beat with at least 3 rises, peak 4-5 at 55-90%, a choice before the peak) instead of thesis, facts and carrier. Numbers are a design, not measured.
usedIn: (none yet: first film of channel post-time-survival; proven by unit tests and a throwaway-episode run)

parts.name: channel-post-text
parts.useWhen: node studio2/post.mjs --episode episodes/<id> writes the one post.txt from POST.json plus the channel's disclosure, footer and hashtags (title max 100 characters).
usedIn: (none yet: first film of channel post-time-survival; proven by unit tests and a throwaway-episode run)

parts.name: music-under-voice-check
parts.useWhen: After writing cues.mjs and before the full render: node studio2/mixcheck.mjs --episode episodes/<id> measures how far the ducked score sits under the narration (aim 10-13 dB; preflight fails outside 8.5-15). Tune scoreVolume in cues.mjs.

parts.name: package-builder
parts.useWhen: Last step of a film, after finish.mjs and the staged cover: node studio2/package.mjs --episode episodes/<id> builds out/publish (final.mp4, cover-small.jpg, post.txt with the channel footer and AI disclosure, metadata.json, package-check.json) and checks decode, length against the channel range, size, black and frozen frames, loudness, peak, title length and files. It never uploads.

parts.name: character-look
parts.useWhen: Every character. createActor reads spec.look: 'ref' (default; flat unlit colour, thick black outline, thick stick arms with round blob hands, thin leg sticks, dark-oval-eye ink face) or 'classic' (older shaded toon). Tune the numbers in LOOKS, never in the scene. Flat 2.5D hair sheets (hair.js), one-piece body painted with collar, hem, seams and an emblem (clothes.js), lens mouth, D-shaped eyes. Hand-drawn line pressure (pen.js): outlines, brows and limbs get heavy/light width; world-space outline in metres.
parts.provenBy: Unit test for the preset table; rendered side by side with the reference (episodes/square-wheel/out/character-look-vs-ref.jpg). Not yet used in a full film, so experimental.

parts.name: model-gate
parts.useWhen: Start of every film's art work: list the models in MODELS.json, build each in scene2/models/<id>.mjs, render its four-view sheet, pass it, only then the next; assemble the scene after all pass.
parts.provenBy: Unit tests for the one-by-one rule; used for the hero of ten-million. Not yet used for a whole film.

parts.name: voice-paragraph-placement
parts.useWhen: A film whose picture is fixed in beats (4 s each) and whose narration must land on them: one voice take, one paragraph per narration line, film.json voiceGaps from the real paragraph lengths, mixSeconds when the last beat is silent.
parts.provenBy: 9 paragraphs placed on their beats (starts 0, 5.15, 12.1, 20.1, 28.1, 36.1, 40.1, 48.1, 52.1 s); mixSeconds made the mix 59.8 s and the gate 1794 frames.

parts.name: multi-zone-world
parts.useWhen: A film that visits several places in 60 s: put each place in its own group 100 m apart, show one per beat, hide the rest, move the sky with the camera, keep one atmosphere table per beat, use zp() only for actors and the camera.
parts.provenBy: Seven zones and an interior set in one film, collide PASS on 1794 frames; sky-follows-camera fixed a pale block, see docs/DEFECTS.json sky-box-fixed-at-origin and zone-child-double-offset. Not yet moved into studio2/library with a test.

parts.name: enterable-prop-models
parts.useWhen: A prop the hero enters or uses: hollow mansion with hall and chandelier, jet with even airstairs and interior set, yacht with a helm station, convertible with a door, speed bump. Copy the staging code (stairH, ramp, hop-over, twist) with them.
parts.provenBy: Used in a delivered film with the collision gate passing; real sizes and lanes in docs/LESSONS.md section G. Not yet moved into studio2/library with tests.

parts.name: story-fun-gate
parts.useWhen: Every new film (film.json funGate true): write the extra STORY.json fields (retell, antagonist, wantResolvedAt, twist, endingTone, weakestBeat, per-beat funny/pressure/fromRule) and run story-audit.mjs before showing or building anything.
parts.provenBy: The old stop-time-hour story failed it with 38 problems; the rewritten story passes; five unit tests cover a flat list of pranks, an early resolved want, a late rival, a sad ending and an early twist.

parts.name: model-fidelity-gate
parts.useWhen: Every model of a new film (film.json fidelityGate true): fill reference, realDetails and interaction in MODELS.json, then pass the model; the tool refuses a modelled value outside its real range.
parts.provenBy: Applied to the 11 models of stop-time-hour it found oversized touch points (remote, watch, pigeon, coffee drop) that were then resized; four unit tests cover in-range, out-of-range, missing data and the opt-in hook.

parts.name: ref-contract
parts.useWhen: Every film: studio2/lib/ref-contract.mjs lists every gate (scaffold turns all on, preflight fails a film that dropped one) and the ordered steps; node studio2/next-step.mjs --episode episodes/<id> prints the first undone step and the session briefing prints it too.

parts.name: camera-plan-gate
parts.useWhen: Before any render: node studio2/camera-plan.mjs reads out/collide.json and fails a shot that does not travel (floor 3% of the frame width per second, reference p10 3.5%, median 13.5%) and a film whose hero is too small (head 12% of the frame in 40% of frames). Reference numbers: python studio2/ref-camera.py (reference/study/camera-travel.json).

parts.name: look-saturation-gate
parts.useWhen: Preflight colour step: median saturation at least .38 and strongly coloured share at least .33 (reference .47 / .47). Engine camera options saturation, skyLow and skyHigh set the grade and the sky colours per shot (dusk, night).

parts.name: realism-layer
parts.useWhen: After a scene is built: texturize(ctx.scene,{THREE}) from /repo/studio2/library/realism.mjs gives every prop procedural PBR surfaces (wood, concrete, asphalt, metal, fabric, tile, plaster, paper, rubber) at real-world tile size; actors stay flat. Preflight's detail step (studio2/detail-check.py against reference/study/detail-stats.json) fails a film under 75% of the reference's fine detail.
